items.summary: On Nov 12-13, Microsoft apologized for a global outage that disrupted services across 74 countries and territories. The company attributed the issue to elevated load during a network capacity upgrade rather than cyber or AI activity. Healthcare systems faced backlogs, airlines reported communication failures, and Copilot outages drew criticism in London's financial district.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupts Services in 74 Countries

items.summary: The Financial Times reported on Nov 13 that Nvidia's board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas in its search for a successor to Jensen Huang, who stepped down on Nov 12 amid revelations of extramarital affairs. Analysts had floated Haas since his exit; he spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013 and became its CEO in 2022. Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while the board weighs candidates.
items.title: Report: Nvidia Approached Arm's Rene Haas as Jensen Huang Successor Candidate

items.summary: A new research effort claims the leading open-weight Chinese AI models were trained on U.S.-export-restricted Blackwell GPUs, underscoring a major problem for chip designer Nvidia. Analysis of model weights by Unemployment Labs' Will DePue found fingerprints suggesting training on banned chips in Moonshot's Kimi K3 and DeepSeek's V4 releases; White House adviser Michael Kratsios also cited intelligence sources implicating Moonshot. Epoch AI estimates roughly 2 million advanced chips entered China through concealment schemes, with about 275,000 Nvidia accelerators routed via Malaysia. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang left amid allegations of an affair with Megaspeed's Alice Huang and possible awareness of smuggling; short-seller Culper argued a 'China problem' threatens Nvidia revenue. Some 600,000 H200 chips are stockpiled in Hong Kong pending clearance.
items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China’s most powerful AI models — uh oh, Jensen!

items.summary: A technical issue during a network capacity upgrade caused a global Microsoft outage lasting nearly 24 hours, affecting more than 70 countries and impacting over 430 million users of products like Outlook, Teams, Exchange Online, and Microsoft 365. Disruption ranged from government services—Japan's government, the Philippines Supreme Court, Australia's spy agency—to hospitals, courts, rail networks in Canada, NHS parts in the UK, US legislative work, and smaller businesses worldwide. Microsoft restored services gradually by Friday afternoon with encouraging progress as email queues normalized. The incident underscored how heavily organizations depend on a handful of big tech providers.
items.title: Microsoft Global Outage Disrupted Services in Over 70 Countries for Nearly 24 Hours

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation from AI chipmaker Nvidia has sent shockwaves through the global economy, following reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Criticism continues to mount over what appears to be a lack of action from US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick, suggesting the fallout remains unresolved.
items.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is far from over - The Latest

items.summary: A widespread outage shut down Microsoft 365 services for businesses, governments, and tens of millions of users worldwide. Beginning around midday Thursday on the East Coast with Outlook failures reported to Downdetector, it quickly spread beyond North America to more than 70 countries. Microsoft ruled out a cyberattack or AI involvement, attributing the incident to an earlier network capacity upgrade following recent changes.
items.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back After a 24-Hour Outage

items.summary: Paul Cristiano of OpenAI's Foundation board and the Alignment Research Center warned at a Toronto lecture series that an 'AI takeover'—where autonomous systems control Earth as humans do, making human intervention futile like opposing the U.S. military—could cause mass death or uninhabitable conditions. Though no model quantifies this risk, he called it a coin flip if AI advances rapidly, with meaningful danger within six to 12 months and 'exceptionally high' odds even amid policy slowdowns.
items.title: OpenAI Board Member Warns AI Takeover Could Be Months Away

items.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday, but congressional questions about his ties to Alice Huang of Megaspeed—a company suspected of funneling restricted AI chips to China—intensify. Three Republican House committee chairs requested testimony in a November 4 letter; Bloomberg and NBC reported he agreed to testify without a subpoena. Lawmakers worry Beijing gained access to sensitive U.S. technology, raising concerns that the Trump administration overlooked espionage warnings.
items.title: Jensen Huang's Resignation Won't End His Congressional Scrutiny

items.summary: The article argues that for most teams, Apache Spark is the better choice because its Real-Time Mode now delivers millisecond end-to-end streaming latency on a single engine that also handles batch ETL, SQL analytics, machine learning, and AI. Previously, Flink's lower latency was the main reason to run it as a second system; with Real-Time Mode closing that gap, teams must instead weigh how many engines they want to build, operate, and govern. Databricks' published benchmark showed Spark matching or beating Flink on stateless workloads and achieving up to 92% lower p99 latency on stateful aggregation and stream-static joins. Production cases like MakeMyTrip report P50 latency of 44 ms and P99 around 500 ms using Real-Time Mode instead of a second engine.
items.title: Apache Spark vs Apache Flink: Choosing Between Unified and Specialized Streaming Engines

items.summary: This walkthrough demonstrates building a beverage-can pick-and-place task in Isaac Sim using UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and beverage can assets from the open SimReady Central library on Hugging Face. The authors introduce SimReady Foundation's three-level structure—Profile, Features, Requirements—and note that validation checks joint-drive settings against profiles such as Robot-Body 4.0.0 and Robot-Gripper 3.0.0. They recommend pre-run tests of joints, movement, contact, and grasp retention before running the task with an agent (GPT-6 Sol) generating Python controls. The scripted run moves the can from a yellow pickup marker to a green target at 4× speed, but results apply only to this fixed setup without vision or robustness guarantees.
items.title: Building a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets in Isaac Sim

items.summary: The resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid extramarital and alleged espionage allegations is expected to tighten US controls on Chinese chip access, possibly reopening debate over banning Chinese AI models. Yet the formal US-China AI safety dialogue—established in September by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Vice Premier He Lifeng with a scheduled Nov. 18-19 meeting between Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen—is likely to continue. Bipartisan congressional support for export restrictions, bipartisan leadership backing NDAA measures, and an administration crackdown on chip diversion suggest sustained pressure on China, though the dialogue itself may proceed independently of these tensions.
items.title: US-China AI Safety Dialogue Holds Despite Huang Scandal

items.summary: In an editorial celebrating M John Harrison's novel The End of Everything as the first science fiction book to win the Booker prize, The Guardian frames the achievement as a breakthrough for a long-marginalised genre. While fans hail it as a victory and critics note its timely relevance amid modern technological anxieties—echoing Ed Miliband's claims that sci-fi scenarios are now reality—Harrison himself resists categorisation, dismissing science fiction labels with iconoclasm. The novel depicts a disintegrating Britain invaded by an alien species called the iGhettis amid capitalism, ecological disaster and AI threats, offering no explanations or salvation.
items.title: The Guardian view on M John Harrison’s Booker win: a new frontier for science fiction | Editorial

items.summary: Engineering teams integrating artificial intelligence face a growing compliance barrier as they translate high-level ethics, governance, and auditing into daily workflows. Traditional degree programs lack training in these areas, making full-time retraining impractical for mid-career engineers. IEEE addresses this gap through its Credentialing Program, which converts decades of standards—most notably the 7000 series on AI system design ethics—into actionable microcredentials that help teams certify systems as safe and compliant within development life cycles.
items.title: How Microcredentials Help Engineers Build Trustworthy AI

items.summary: The Electrek Podcast previews its weekly sustainable transport and energy episode, airing live every Friday at 4 p.m. ET on YouTube with an accompanying site post and embedded stream link. After the show ends around 5 p.m., the video is archived online while audio remains available across podcast apps.
items.title: Podcast: Tesla trims are falling like flies, Hyundai 2027 lineup, and BYD’s Rolls-Royce

items.summary: Tesla now sells only the tri-motor Cyberbeast in the US, which rose to $109,990 after a recent $7,500 increase. The Dual Motor AWD ($82,490) and Premium AWD ($92,490) trims remain listed but are no longer orderable, making the Cyberbeast the sole purchasable version at 57% above its early-August price of $69,990. Elon Musk announced production would end on November 6 while extending it through summer 2027 to clear backlog; Tesla estimates delivered roughly 30,000 units annually against over 125,000 installed capacity.
items.title: Tesla Cybertruck Price Hikes and Trim Cuts Amid Production Wind-Down

items.summary: Environmental groups say the recently discovered, two-inch-long Birmingham darter—found in only six small streams near Bessemer and Tuscaloosa—is functionally endangered. The Alabama Rivers Alliance, Center for Biological Diversity and Black Warrior Riverkeeper petitioned the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service nearly a year ago to list it under the Endangered Species Act; they say FWS missed its 90-day interim-decision deadline. With land already cleared for Project Marvel—a 4.5-million-square-foot QTS data center in Bessemer bought for $432 million—the groups sent notice of intent to sue, threatening court if no response arrives within 60 days. The darter's habitat also faces the Birmingham Northern Beltline highway project and decades of industrial pollution.
items.title: Trump Administration Stalling Protections for Imperiled Fish Near Massive Alabama Data Center, Groups Say

items.summary: Voluntary water conservation programs in the Upper Colorado River Basin are progressing after the 320th meeting of the Upper Colorado River Commission, though states and the federal government still cannot agree on how conserved water would be credited and stored. In June, Reclamation offered $100 million to fund upper-basin state programs that typically pay ranchers and farmers to use less water. Most states plan implementation in 2027. Colorado insists its program proceed only if conserved water stays under state jurisdiction; Utah already runs one and saved about 5,500 acre feet in 2025. Reclamation modeled up to 200,000 acre feet of annual upper-basin conservation. Negotiators remain years from a federal operating agreement after missing deadlines.
items.title: Upper Colorado River Conservation Programs Advance Amid Unresolved Credit and Storage Questions

items.summary: Canary Media's Jeff St. John reflects on the midterm elections' expansion of Democratic power and its implications for clean energy in California, following his fourth annual Canary Live Bay Area event that drew nearly 400 people to Berkeley. Guest Leah Stokes criticized outgoing Gov. Gavin Newsom over clawing back $200 million in school heating funding amid extreme classroom heat and undercutting the Demand Side Grid Support program, which disproportionately benefits lower-income Central Valley and Inland Empire residents. She expressed optimism about incoming Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra's focus on affordability and environmental justice, favoring his free 'Power Hour' solar proposal. The article also covers a Bay Area Air District vote restricting gas-fueled water heaters from 2028.
items.title: How California Gov.-elect Becerra Could Be Better on Climate Than Newsom

items.summary: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey opened as an 'implementation' conference focused on turning past climate pledges into action rather than new promises. Indigenous advocates view it as a test of whether commitments to protect land rights across 400 million acres and provide $1.8 billion in funding will materialize. Frustration persists: Nepal's first loss-and-damage disbursement reached only $21.6 million, less than 1 percent of its $5 billion damage. Speakers like Edward Porokwa stress that responsibility for climate action falls on smaller nations and Indigenous peoples, while a UN report says limiting warming to 1.5 degrees is now virtually impossible.
items.title: Indigenous Leaders at COP31 Demand Climate Promises Turn Into Action

items.summary: An analysis by DeKleptocracy found Trump bought $1m–$5m of Nvidia stock as his administration rescinded a rule blocking advanced US AI chips from China in May 2025. Nvidia shares rose after the announcement, and he made further purchases between December 2025 and January 2026 to allow H200 chip sales—six times better than what was available in China at the time.
items.title: Trump's Nvidia Stock Purchases Amid China Export Rule Changes

items.summary: Ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned after reports of extramarital affairs involving a suspected Chinese spy, has engaged law firm Paul Weiss amid his downfall. The New York-based firm, with more than 1,500 lawyers, previously struck a controversial $40 million pro bono deal with Trump and faced scrutiny over its longtime chairman Brad Karp's Epstein ties; Reuters could not confirm which attorneys represent Huang.
items.title: Nvidia's Huang turns to Paul Weiss, law firm that inked deal with Trump

items.summary: This week's internet was dominated by AI-generated memes about Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, whose extramarital affairs prompted his resignation. The humor ironically relied on Nvidia chips while he faced the fallout of wiping hundreds of billions in investor value. Meme traffic also surged over a 12-hour Microsoft outage affecting Outlook and Teams.
items.title: AI Meme Storm Overshadowed Jensen Huang Scandal and Microsoft Outage

items.summary: This Semafor report alleges that Nvidia, under co-founder Jensen Huang and general counsel Tim Teter, exerted unprecedented influence over US chip export controls. In January, Teter reportedly told government officials—citing President Trump—that proposed license conditions on H200 chips to China should be dropped quickly, calling a cloud-customer requirement a 'poison pill.' Staffers accuse the company of gaslighting Congress and misrepresenting technical feasibility, including falsely claiming location-verification technology was impossible before launching it in May. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is described as a compliant partner focused on avoiding trade friction. The allegations gained weight after Huang resigned amid reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy; Nvidia's market value reportedly fell $1.5 trillion.
items.title: How Nvidia's Jensen Huang – and Trump – Jumped the Guardrails

items.summary: Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia may disrupt the rollout of AI across Africa, where chips remain essential. The exit raises questions about Nvidia's partnership with Cassava Technologies and its supply role in more than 30 African countries. Implications extend to South Africa, home to roughly 40% of the continent's ~160 data centers.
items.title: Nvidia CEO’s Exit Marks Pivotal Moment for African AI

items.summary: Nvidia is navigating a leadership transition after CEO Jensen Huang exits, drawing attention to Aarti Shah, an Indian-origin executive and former senior leader at Eli Lilly who joined the board in 2020. She is among directors involved in selecting his successor. The development highlights her career spanning statistics, pharmaceutical research, digital transformation, and corporate governance.
items.title: Aarti Shah Among Nvidia Directors Considering Jensen Huang's Successor

items.summary: The Trump administration is weighing removing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick amid an Nvidia chip-export dispute with China. Megaspark reportedly bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips from June 2024, allegedly routed to China through executive Alice Huang, linked to the Ministry of State Security and ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation.
items.title: ट्रंप प्रशासन से होगी हॉवर्ड लटनिक की छुट्टी? Nvidia विवाद और चीन कनेक्शन से बढ़ीं मुश्किलें

items.summary: Microsoft apologized for a global outage affecting services in 74 countries and territories, attributing the disruption to an earlier network capacity upgrade rather than cyber or AI activity. The incident knocked out products including Outlook and Copilot, disrupting health care referrals in the UK, visa processing in New Zealand, airline support in India, and corporate communications worldwide.
items.title: Microsoft Outage Disrupts Services Across 74 Countries

items.summary: Microsoft apologized for a global outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Microsoft 365 across 74 countries and territories. The company attributed the disruption to elevated load during a network capacity upgrade, ruling out cyber or AI causes, while reporting broad recovery. Healthcare services, corporate earnings deadlines and schools were disrupted; airlines in India, Immigration New Zealand and Japan's economy minister cited significant impacts.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes for Global Outage Amid Broad Recovery of Services

items.summary: Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia sent the company's value tumbling, shedding 14 per cent intraday before closing down almost 5 per cent. Since October 6, Nvidia has lost 30 per cent of its value as scandal over alleged romantic ties to a suspected Chinese spy compounded fears that higher interest rates and political shifts would slow AI rollout. Economist magazine called it possibly the most expensive affair in history. Huang's concentrated control—60 direct reports with no successor plan—has left the company exposed, prompting interim leadership from CFO Colette Kress. With Nvidia worth $US4.5 trillion and more than $1 trillion of Australian superannuation invested offshore, investors face mounting uncertainty over a pivotal moment for AI.
items.title: Why You Will Pay for Jensen Huang's Indiscretions

items.summary: A major outage hit Microsoft on Thursday, affecting Outlook, Teams, and Copilot services across more than 70 countries and millions of users. Fix attempts reportedly failed as expected, keeping the issue unresolved through Friday. The public responded with humor, trending "Microsoft" online and joking that employees should take their time—comparing it to a snow day for adults or Avengers: Doomsday.
items.title: Funniest Reactions to Microsoft's Global Outage

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reported on Friday that European diesel prices remain about 77% above pre-war levels, though crude (North Sea Dated) fell from $136 to roughly $93 and diesel dropped ~11% to nearly $180. Global oil supply exceeded demand for the first time since the Iran war began as Gulf exports recovered; global supply reached 105.4 million barrels per day while demand is forecast to fall to 102.3 million this year, with recovery expected in 2027.
items.title: IEA Reports European Diesel Prices Remain High as Global Oil Supply Overtakes Demand

items.summary: Senator Chris Van Hollen said he will no longer pursue a 2028 presidential run as challengers to Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader emerge. Peggy Flanagan backs him; Elissa Slotkin is weighing it seriously but won’t support Schumer, while Julianna Stratton declines to endorse either.
items.title: Van Hollen rules out 2028 presidential bid amid Democratic leadership contest and post-election news

items.summary: A tanker struck the American Heritage river cruise ship, carrying about 129 people plus crew near Port of New Orleans. The vessel took on water and began sinking; rescue efforts continue as officials hold a press conference.
items.title: Tanker Collides with River Cruise Ship in New Orleans

items.summary: Democratic Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer faces a leadership challenge from fellow Senator Chris Van Hollen, who argues the party needs new leadership to deliver after midterm victories. Left-wing Democrats view Schumer as too moderate and part of the establishment. The contested vote will occur behind closed doors in early December, with the winner assuming office on 4 January when Democrats take control of both chambers.
items.title: Schumer Faces Leadership Challenge from Van Hollen as Democrats Prepare for Midterm Sweep

items.summary: Nine months into the war with Iran, President Trump is confronting dwindling options for ending the conflict and appears to favor maintaining the status quo. He dismissed a deal as unnecessary, citing billions of frozen Iranian dollars, while Gulf allies prefer continued economic pressure over escalation. With midterm losses blamed on the unpopular war and Israel relations, his maneuvering room has narrowed. Iran remains defiant, insisting seven demands be met before nuclear talks. The conflict continues to strain regional economies—Gulf states face recession—with tit-for-tat strikes persisting as mediators struggle to bridge divides between locked sides.}**visual**: {
items.title: Trump's Strategy With Iran Is To Keep Things As They Are

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV celebrated mass on Friday at a park near Pimentel, about 10km from Chiclayo in northern Peru. The Vatican estimates more than 1.5 million people gathered to welcome the pontiff during his Latin America tour. Many arrived after long waits in heat past 30C; some came from across Peru and neighbouring countries. For locals, the event carries deep meaning: Leo lived here between 1985 and 2023, became a Peruvian citizen in 2015, and served as bishop of Chiclayo until 2023. Former colleagues recall his compassion for migrants and poor communities, soup kitchens during Covid-19, and efforts to bring people together. The city's usual population of around 800,000 is estimated to have doubled for the visit.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Returns Home for Mass in Chiclayo

items.summary: This week's briefing covers three stories: the downfall of Jensen Huang, dubbed the Taylor Swift of AI, whose scandalous headlines cost him his job. In geopolitics, the first direct talks between Ukraine and Russia since February occurred with the US in the room while Europeans were relegated to the lobby per Moscow. Meanwhile, European protests continue, including Spain's first general strike in 14 years over housing and living costs.
items.title: The Downfall of AI's 'Rock Star' Boss; Ukraine Talks and European Protests

items.summary: Honduras declared a 36-month environmental emergency for the Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve, its largest protected area. The decree allocates 1.5 billion lempiras (over $55 million) over three years to combat deforestation and crime in this remote reserve spanning Gracias a Dios, Colón and Olancho departments. At least 6,691 hectares were cleared between 2023 and 2025. Environmental groups question whether funding will translate into real enforcement action.
items.title: Honduras Declares Environmental Emergency in Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve

items.summary: Lecturer Alexander Titov discusses high-level meetings in Abu Dhabi and Dublin regarding the war in Ukraine. He notes Russia wants negotiations to extend beyond a ceasefire, covering territory, NATO membership, and post-war relations with other countries. Europe lacks a unified voice, making it difficult to agree on negotiating priorities. While there is some hope for wider post-war arrangements, Titov cautions against expecting an imminent breakthrough, as Russia shows no urgency.
items.title: Europe's Divergent Positions Complicate Ukraine Peace Prospects as Russia Stalls on Negotiations

items.summary: This CGTN trailer explores how Shenzhen transformed from a small fishing village into one of China's most dynamic cities, with GDP rising more than 10,000-fold and exports ranking first among Chinese cities for 33 consecutive years. Former World Bank country director Bert Hofman and author Zak Dychtwald investigate the city's remarkable rise by meeting young people shaping its future across studios, factories, and competition arenas. The documentary premieres November 17th.
items.title: Trailer｜Shenzhen: The making of a miracle

items.summary: A viral X map claiming China has blockaded and annexed Taiwan is misleading; Beijing deployed significant forces since November 2 but simulated, not enforced, a blockade. Analyst Emmanuel Véron calls the claim false, citing influencer exaggeration or propaganda. The account sharing the map, Fablex, appears to be a clickbait operation based in Uganda rather than California. Official figures show sharp declines: aircraft detections fell from 49 on November 3 to just one over November 8-9, and ships dropped to eight—insufficient for a blockade. Véron notes this is an unprecedented multi-front naval exercise involving about 100 vessels, likely aimed at communication games ahead of the APEC summit in China.
items.title: Debunking Claims of a Chinese Blockade Around Taiwan

items.summary: A controversy involving Jensen Huang, a businesswoman suspected of spying for China who worked at Singapore-based Megaspeed, has prompted US lawmakers from both parties to push stronger restrictions on China's access to advanced AI chips. Lawmakers seek to close loopholes allowing Chinese firms to rent overseas computing power with restricted Nvidia chips. Proposed rules could add export controls and licensing requirements for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore. Southeast Asia's data-centre industry has expanded rapidly—Malaysia approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of related investment since 2021—and the AI boom is supporting regional growth. Some analysts expect tighter rules could harm prospects, while others believe expansion will continue.
items.title: Jensen Huang Controversy and Tightening AI Chip Controls in Southeast Asia

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has approved the appointment of Pratap Singh as MD and CEO of Fino Payments Bank (FPB) for three years, effective November 27, 2026. Singh brings over 29 years of experience across retail banking, SME banking, digital transformation and operating model redesign in institutions including ICICI Bank, ICICI Bank UK and SBI UK. The bank's Board will proceed with the appointment pending shareholder approval; FPB said it would notify stock exchanges once he formally takes charge. Ketan Merchant has led FPB as interim CEO since February 2026.
items.title: RBI Approves Appointment of Pratap Singh as MD & CEO of Fino Payments Bank

items.summary: Microsoft apologized for a global outage that knocked Outlook, Teams and Copilot offline for millions of users for much of a day. The company attributed the disruption to an earlier network capacity upgrade whose fault surfaced after a recent change, explicitly ruling out cyber or AI causes. Reports arrived from 74 countries within about an hour; India saw spikes around 11:21 pm local time on Thursday. Anderson Economic Group estimated lost productivity could reach close to $7 billion and that as many as 51 million users were disrupted Friday alone. Recovery was gradual, with North America recovering faster than Europe and Asia.
items.title: Microsoft Apologizes and Explains Outlook, Teams Outage

items.summary: Jensen Huang's ouster from Nvidia has drawn intense support, though it may not reverse like OpenAI's 2023 removal of Sam Altman. An internal post attracted more than 1,600 comments—mostly favoring his return—but these are suggestions, not a formal petition or mass threat. Silicon Valley voices echoed the sentiment: Elon Musk called reinstatement an honor; Tim Sweeney likened firing Huang to Apple dismissing Steve Jobs; Palmer Luckey and Aravind Srinivas praised his leadership. Yet Nvidia's situation differs fundamentally. Unlike Altman's governance dispute, Huang's departure follows national-security concerns, prompting interim CEO Colette Kress and a search for a permanent successor.
items.title: Will Jensen Huang Get a Comeback Like Sam Altman?

items.summary: Microsoft reported Friday that it completed recovery actions across affected infrastructure in the Asia Pacific region and is gradually restoring traffic, though Microsoft 365 services including Outlook email remained disrupted for a second day. The company cited unexpected server unavailability rather than increased traffic as the cause, with no evidence of malicious activity.
items.title: Microsoft Gradually Restores Asia Pacific Services After Second-Day Outage

items.summary: Google announced its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, now available globally across Google Search and all tiers of AI Studio, the API, Business, the app, and paid Antigravity subscribers. Robby Stein noted it is the default in AI Mode and delivers more visual responses with comparison tables and charts. The model offers significant speed and intelligence gains over Gemini Flash 3.8 and matches or beats Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.
items.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen Model for Complex Queries

items.summary: India posted record goods exports of about $90 billion in October, per the Commerce Ministry. The merchandise trade deficit nonetheless widened to a one-year high of $39.88 billion—above estimates—as festive demand and higher oil prices lifted imports. Services remained in surplus at roughly $40.51 billion against $20.72 billion in imports.
items.title: India's October Exports Hit Record $90 Billion as Merchandise Deficit Widens

items.summary: The Delhi High Court directed its registry to seek explanations from a trial court judge, the chief judicial magistrate (CJM) and district judge over failure to pronounce an order pending since April 22, 2026. Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora sought clarification on staff shortage and backlog of over 4,500 cases cited for delay. The matter stems from a petition filed by Pradeep Bansal under Article 227 seeking time-bound disposal of an application dated April 8, 2024. Arguments were completed Jan 6, 2026 but the order remained unpronounced since April 22 and deferred four times most recently Oct 27.
items.title: 1 stenographer, 4,500 cases: HC seeks explanation over delay in pronouncing order

items.summary: Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat expressed hope that Pakistan would join the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in Delhi (Nov 20-22), while dismissing Pakistan's attempt to claim the ~5,000-year-old Indus Valley civilisation. He noted Pakistan came into existence only around 80 years ago and became separate from India after Partition in 1947.
items.title: India's Culture Minister Rejects Pakistan's Indus Valley Civilisation Claims Ahead of SCO Forum

items.summary: A new version of the 1968 film, remade in 1999, will release in cinemas on March 5, 2027. Directed by Michael B Jordan, who also stars alongside Adria Arjona, the cast includes Pilou Asbæk and Kenneth Branagh.
items.title: 'The Thomas Crown Affair' Trailer Announced; Michael B Jordan Directs and Stars in Reboot

items.summary: Uttarakhand released its draft electoral roll on November 12, listing 72,78,035 voters following a Special Intensive Revision (SIR) campaign from October 4 to 31. The count rose by 1,19,086 from the earlier figure of 71,58,949 on October 3. Claims and objections remain open until December 11, with final publication scheduled for January 4.
items.title: Uttarakhand Releases Draft Voter List After Special Revision

items.summary: A Missouri appeals court ruled that a couple who transferred title of their wrecked 2018 Lexus to an unidentified tow-truck driver no longer owned the vehicle and remained liable for its $6,450 towing bill. The Keeners signed over ownership in 2018 but later argued they had already given away the car and should not pay storage or related fees. Somerset Apartment Management maintained that the signature did not complete a legal transfer without proper state recording, yet contended the couple benefited from services rendered. Applying estoppel, the court found their conduct demonstrated abandonment of ownership and declined to let them back out after delay.
items.title: Missouri Couple Escapes $6,450 Towing Bill After Giving Away Wrecked Lexus
